title: Combinatorial geometry
summary: Finite point sets in the plane: how many unit distances, how many distinct distances, when points must contain a convex $k$-gon, how lines and points can be incident.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #846
research_problems.statement:
Let `A ⊂ ℝ²` be an infinite set for which there exists some `ϵ>0` such that in any subset of `A`
of size `n` there are always at least `ϵn` with no three on a line.
Is it true that `A` is the union of a finite number of sets where no three are on a line?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #798
research_problems.statement:
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the $\binom{t}{2}$
lines determined by these points cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.

Estimate $t(n)$. In particular, is it true that $t(n)=o(n)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #503
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every three points from $A$
determine an isosceles triangle? That is, for any three points $x$, $y$, $z$ from $A$, at least two
of the distances $|x - y|$, $|y - z|$, $|x - z|$ are equal.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #352
research_problems.statement:
Is there some $c > 0$ such that every measurable $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of measure $\geq c$
 contains the vertices of a triangle of area 1?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #654
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n)$ be such that, given any $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ with no four points on a
circle, there exists some $x_i$ with at least $f(n)$ many distinct distances to the other $x_j$.
Is it true that $f(n) > (1-o(1))n$?

(b) Let $f(n)$ be as in `erdos_654.parts.i`. Is it true that $f(n) > (\frac{1}{3}+c)n$ for some
constant $c>0$ and all large $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #96
research_problems.statement:
If $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then there are $O(n)$ many pairs which are
distance $1$ apart.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #214
research_problems.statement:
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no two points in $S$ are distance $1$ apart. Must the
complement of $S$ contain four points which form a unit square?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #91
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1121
research_problems.statement:
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #657
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a set of $n$ points such that every subset of $3$
points determines $3$ distinct distances (that is, $A$ has no isosceles triangles, degenerate
ones included) then $A$ determines at least $f(n)n$ distinct distances, for some function $f$
with $f(n)\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1207
research_problems.statement: Let $P_d(n)$ be such that in any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exist at least $P_d(n)$ many points which do not contain an isosceles triangle. Estimate $P_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$P_2(n)<n^{1-c}$$ for some constant $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1089
research_problems.statement:
Let $g_d(n)$ be minimal such that every collection of $g_d(n)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines
at least $n$ many distinct distances. Estimate $g_d(n)$. In particular, does
$$\lim_{d \to \infty} \frac{g_d(n)}{d^{n-1}}$$
exist?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #633
research_problems.statement: Which triangles can only be decomposed into a square number of congruent triangles?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1083
research_problems.statement: Let $d\geq 3$, and let $f_d(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines at least $m$ distinct distances. Estimate $f_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$f_d(n)=n^{\frac{2}{d}-o(1)}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #670
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points such that all pairwise distances differ by
at least $1$. Is the diameter of $A$ at least $(1+o(1))n^2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #757
research_problems.statement: What is the supremum of the set of admissible numbers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #353
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a measurable set with infinite measure. Must $A$ contain the
vertices of an isosceles trapezoid of area $1$? What about an isosceles triangle, or a
right-angled triangle, or a cyclic quadrilateral, or a convex polygon with congruent sides?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #189
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #95
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb{R}^2$ determine the set of distances $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose
$u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of points. Then for all $\epsilon>0$
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll_\epsilon n^{3+\epsilon}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1088
research_problems.statement:
Let $f_d(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that any set of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a set of
$n$ points for which any two determined distances are distinct. Erdős Problem 1088 asks to
estimate $f_d(n)$. In particular, is it true that, for every fixed $n \geq 3$,
$$
f_d(n) = 2^{o(d)}
$$
as $d \to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #102
research_problems.statement:
Let $c > 0$ and let $h_c(n)$ be such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least
$cn^2$ lines that each contain more than three of the points, some line contains $h_c(n)$ of
the points. Is it true that, for fixed $c > 0$, $h_c(n) \to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1087
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains at most $f(n)$
many sets of four points which are 'degenerate' in the sense that some pair are the same distance
apart. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #588
research_problems.statement:
Let $f_k(n)$ be minimal such that if $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ have no $k+1$ points on a line
then there must be at most $f_k(n)$ many lines containing at least $k$ points. Is it true that
$$f_k(n) = o(n^2)$$
for $k \geq 4$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #505
research_problems.statement:
(disproved). Borsuk's conjecture is false for
sufficiently large $n$: there exists a dimension $n$ and a bounded set
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with at least two points that cannot be
covered by $n + 1$ subsets each of strictly smaller diameter.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #224
research_problems.statement: If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is any set of $2^d+1$ points then some three points in $A$ determine an obtuse angle.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1071
research_problems.statement:
(a) Can a finite set of disjoint unit segments in a unit square be maximal?
Solved affirmatively by [Da85], who gave an explicit construction.

(b) Is there a region $R$ with a maximal set of disjoint unit line segments that is countably infinite?
Here a unit line segment is a rotated and translated copy of the open interval $(0,1)$, and it is
required to be contained in $R$.
Solved affirmatively by [Fo99], who gave an explicit construction.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #668
research_problems.statement:
(a) Is it true that the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximise the
number of unit distances tends to infinity as $n\to\infty$?

(b) Is it always $>1$ for $n>3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1086
research_problems.statement:
Let $g(n)$ be minimal such that any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of
at most $g(n)$ many triangles with the same area. Estimate $g(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #103
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(n)$ count the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which minimise
the diameter subject to the constraint that $d(x,y)\geq 1$ for all points $x\neq y$. Is it true
that $h(n)\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #504
research_problems.statement:
For $n \ge 3$,
$\alpha_{2^n} = \pi\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #653
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #211
research_problems.statement:
Let $1\leq k<n$. Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, at most $n-k$ on any line,
there are $\gg kn$ many lines which contain at least two points.
Solved by Beck [Be83] and Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83].

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #97
research_problems.statement: Does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #210
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n)$ be the sharp guarantee such that, for any $n$ points in $\mathbb R^2$,
not all on a line, there are at least $f(n)$ lines which contain exactly two points
(called ordinary lines). Does $f(n)\to\infty$?
That $f(n)\to\infty$ was proved by Motzkin [Mo51].

(b) How fast does $f(n)$ tend to infinity? Kelly–Moser [KeMo58] and the near-pencil
construction show that its growth is linear.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #94
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determine a convex polygon and the set of distances between
them is $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose $u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of
points. Then
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #193
research_problems.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^3$ be a finite set and let $A = \lbrace a_1, a_2, \ldots \rbrace$ be
an infinite $S$-walk, so that $a_{i+1} - a_i \in S$ for all $i$. Must $A$ contain three collinear
points?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #704
research_problems.statement:
(a) Does $\chi(G_n)$ grow exponentially in $n$?

(b) Let $G_n$ be the unit distance graph in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with two vertices joined by an edge if
and only if the distance between them is $1$. Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\chi(G_n)^{1/n}$$
exist?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #188
research_problems.statement:
What is the smallest $k$ such that $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be red/blue coloured with no pair of red
points unit distance apart, and no $k$-term arithmetic progression of blue points with distance 1?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #652
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let
$R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$, where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $\alpha_k$ be minimal such that, for all large enough $n$, there exists a set of $n$ points
with $R(x_k)<\alpha_kn^{1/2}$. Is it true that $\alpha_k\to \infty$ as $k\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1090
research_problems.statement: Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #769
research_problems.statement:
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #105
research_problems.statement:
Let $A,B\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be disjoint sets of size $n$ and $n-3$ respectively, with not all
of $A$ contained on a single line. Is there a line which contains at least two points from $A$
and no points from $B$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #756
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Can there be $\gg n$ many distinct distances
each of which occurs for more than $n$ many pairs from $A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #90
research_problems.statement:
Does every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contain at most
$n^{1+O(\frac{1}{\log\log n})}$ many pairs which are distance $1$ apart?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #101
research_problems.statement:
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no five of which are on a line, the number of
lines containing four points is $o(n^2)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #659
research_problems.statement:
Is there a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every subset of $4$ points determines at
least $3$ distances, yet the total number of distinct distances is $\ll \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #209
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite collection of $d\geq 4$ non-parallel lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
there are no points where at least four lines from $A$ meet. Must there exist a 'Gallai
triangle' (or 'ordinary triangle'): three lines from $A$ which intersect in three points, and
each of these intersection points only intersects two lines from $A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #212
research_problems.statement:
Is there a dense subset of ℝ^2 such that all pairwise distances
are rational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #898
research_problems.statement:
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #502
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ such that there are only two distinct
distances between elements of $A$? That is,
$$\# \{ \lvert x-y\rvert : x\neq y\in A\} = 2.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #959
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of size $n$ and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be
the set of distinct distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the number of times
the distance $d$ is determined, ordered so that
$f(d_1)\geq f(d_2)\geq \cdots \geq f(d_k)$. Estimate
$$\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2)),$$
where the maximum is taken over all $A$ of size $n$ (this is `extremalGap n`).

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #755
research_problems.statement:
Erdős asked whether every $n$-point set in
$\mathbb{R}^6$ spans at most $(1/27 + o(1)) n^3$ unit equilateral triangles.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #655
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no circle whose centre is one
of the $x_i$ contains three other points. Are there at least
$$(1+c)\frac{n}{2}$$
distinct distances determined between the $x_i$, for some constant $c>0$ and
all $n$ sufficiently large?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #100
research_problems.statement: Is the diameter of $A$ at least $Cn$ for some constant $C > 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #99
research_problems.statement:
For sufficiently large n, is it the case that any set of n points with minimum distance $1$
that minimizes diameter must contain an equilateral triangle of side length 1?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #89
research_problems.statement:
Erdős [Er46] asked whether every set of $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$
determines $\gg \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #107
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that any $f(n)$ points in $ℝ^2$, no three on a line,
contain $n$ points which form the vertices of a convex $n$-gon.
Prove that $f(n) = 2^{n-2} + 1$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #93
research_problems.statement:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then they determine at least
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ distinct distances.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #174
research_problems.statement:
A finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Ramsey if, for any $k\geq 1$, there exists some
$d=d(A,k)$ such that in any $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a monochromatic copy
of $A$. Characterise the Ramsey sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #958
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of size $n$, and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be the set of
distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the multiplicity of $d$, that is, the number of
unordered pairs from $A$ of distance $d$ apart.

Is it true that $k=n-1$ and $\{f(d_i)\}=\{n-1,\ldots,1\}$ if and only if $A$ is a set of
equidistant points on a line or a circle?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #98
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #173
research_problems.statement:
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$ (up to
congruence), there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1069
research_problems.statement:
Given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the number of $k$-rich lines (lines which contain
$\geq k$ of the points) is, provided $k\leq n^{1/2}$,
$$\ll \frac{n^2}{k^3}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #604
research_problems.statement:
Given $n$ distinct points $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, must there be a point $x\in A$ such that
$$\#\{ d(x,y) : y \in A\} \gg n^{1-o(1)}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #215
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that every set congruent to $S$ (that is, $S$
after some translation and rotation) contains exactly one point from $\mathbb{Z}^2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #661
research_problems.statement:
Are there, for all large $n$, some points $x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ such that
the number of distinct distances $d(x_i,y_j)$ is
$$o\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}\right)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #982
research_problems.statement:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1082
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?

(b) Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Must there exist a single point from which there are at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct
distances?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #669
research_problems.statement:
Let $F_k(n)$ be minimal such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exist at most
$F_k(n)$ many distinct lines passing through at least $k$ of the points, and $f_k(n)$ similarly
but with lines passing through exactly $k$ points.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #213
research_problems.statement:
Let $n \geq 4$. Are there $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #104
research_problems.statement: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ the number of distinct unit circles containing at least three points is $o(n^2)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #827
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_k$ be minimal such that if $n_k$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ are in general position then
there exists a subset of $k$ points such that all $\binom{k}{3}$ triples determine circles of
different radii.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #660
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in \mathbb{R}^3$ be the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Are there at least
$$(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$$
many distinct distances between the $x_i$?

title: Infinite combinatorics and partition calculus
summary: Ramsey theory for infinite sets and cardinals. The arrow notation $\kappa \to (\lambda)^n_r$ asks whether every colouring of $n$-subsets of $\kappa$ with $r$ colours has a homogeneous set of size $\lambda$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #596
research_problems.statement:
(Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

(1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1176
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1219
research_problems.statement:
Let $(n_k)$ be an increasing sequence of integers such that $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ is strictly
increasing, and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$. Is it true that
$$\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #598
research_problems.statement:
Let $\kappa = (2^{\aleph_0})^+$. This is the successor cardinal of the continuum.

**Erdős Problem 598:**
Let $m$ be an infinite cardinal and $\kappa$ be the successor cardinal of $2^{\aleph_0}$.
Can one colour the countable subsets of $m$ using $\kappa$ many colours so that every
$X \subseteq m$ with $|X| = \kappa$ contains subsets of all possible colours?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1119
research_problems.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal with $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{m} < \mathfrak{c} =
2^{\aleph_0}$. Let $\{f_\alpha\}$ be a family of entire functions such that, for every
$z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$, there are at most $\mathfrak{m}$ distinct values of $f_\alpha(z_0)$.
Must $\{f_\alpha\}$ have cardinality at most $\mathfrak{m}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #593
research_problems.statement:
Characterize those finite 3-uniform hypergraphs which appear
in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number $> \aleph_0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #592
research_problems.statement:
Determine which countable ordinals $β$ have the property that, if $α = \omega^β$, then in any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #595
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite graph $G$ which contains no $K_4$ and is
not the union of countably many triangle-free graphs?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #70
research_problems.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{c}$ be the order type of the real numbers,
let $\beta$ be a countable ordinal, and let $2 \le n < \omega$.
Is it true that $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #623
research_problems.statement:
Let $X$ be a set of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$ and $f$ be a function from the finite subsets of
$X$ to $X$ such that $f(A)\not\in A$ for all $A$. Must there exist an infinite $Y\subseteq X$

\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2 \sum_{n, m \in A: n < m \leq x}
\frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\to\infty
$$
as $x\to\infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #452
research_problems.statement:
Determine the largest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #433
research_problems.statement:
For every fixed $k \geq 2$, Erdős and Graham conjectured that
$$g(k,n) \sim \frac{n^2}{k-1}.$$
The conjecture was proved by Dixmier [Di90].

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #841
research_problems.statement:
Let $t_n$ be minimal such that $\{n+1,\ldots,n+t_n\}$ contains a subset whose product with $n$ is
a square number (and let $t_n=0$ if $n$ is itself square). Estimate $t_n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #246
research_problems.statement: Let $(a,b)=1$. The set $\{a^kb^l: k,l\geq 0\}$ is complete - that is, every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^kb^l$ with $k,l\geq 0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #332
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and $D(A)$ be the set of those numbers which occur infinitely often as
$a_1 - a_2$ with $a_1, a_2\in A$. What conditions on $A$ are sufficient to ensure $D(A)$ has bounded
gaps?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1106
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$\prod_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, then $F(n)$ tends to infinity when $n$ tends to infinity.

(b) Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$\prod_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, $F(n)>n$ for sufficiently large $n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #695
research_problems.statement:
Let $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of primes such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$. Is it
true that
$$
\lim_{k \to \infty} q_k^{1/k} = \infty?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #254
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert -\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \to
\infty\textrm{ as }x\to \infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}=\infty$ for every $\theta\in
(0,1)$, where $\{x\}$ is the distance of $x$ from the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of distinct elements of $A$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #648
research_problems.statement:
Let $g(n)$ denote the largest $t$ such that there exist integers $2\leq a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_t <n$
such that $$P(a_1)>P(a_2)>\cdots >P(a_t)$$ where $P(m)$ is the greatest prime factor of $m$.
Estimate $g(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1060
research_problems.statement:
(a) The conjecture is about the function $f(n)$ which counts the number of solutions to
$k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. The first bound is that $f(n)$ grows slower
than any power of $n^(\frac{1}{\log\log n})$. The second bound is that $f(n)$ is at most a power of
$\log n$.

(b) Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1180
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #913
research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that if
$$
  n(n + 1) = \prod_i p_i^{k_i}
$$
is the factorisation into distinct primes then all exponents $k_i$ are distinct?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #261
research_problems.statement:
(a) Are there infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that there exist some $t \ge 2$ and
distinct integers $a_1, \ldots, a_t \ge 1$ satisfying
$$\frac{n}{2^n} = \sum_{1 \le k \le t} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}?$$

(b) Do all positive integers $n$ have the required property?

(c) Is there a rational number $x$ such that
$$x = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}$$
has at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ representations by pairwise distinct positive integers $a_k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #541
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_1, \dots, a_p$ be (not necessarily distinct) residues modulo a prime $p$, such that there
exists some $r$ so that if $S \subseteq [p]$ is non-empty and
$$\sum_{i \in S} a_i \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$$
then $|S| = r$.

Must there be at most two distinct residues amongst the $a_i$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #663
research_problems.statement:
Let $k \geq 2$, and let $q(n,k)$ denote the least prime which does not divide
$\prod_{1 \leq i \leq k}(n+i)$. Is it true that, if $k$ is fixed and $n$ is sufficiently
large, then $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\log n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #679
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\epsilon>0$ and $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct prime factors of $n$.
Are there infinitely many values of $n$ such that
$$\omega(n-k) < (1+\epsilon)\frac{\log k}{\log\log k}$$
for all $k<n$ which are sufficiently large depending on $\epsilon$ only?

(b) Can one show the stronger version with
$$\omega(n-k) < \frac{\log k}{\log\log k}+O(1)$$
is false?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #34
research_problems.statement:
For any permutation $\pi\in S_n$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $S(\pi)$ count the number of distinct consecutive sums, that is, sums of the shape $\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}\pi(i)$. Is it true that
$$
S(\pi) = o(n^2)
$$
for all $\pi\in S_n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #38
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist $B \subset \mathbb{N}$ which is not an additive basis,
but is such that for every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of Schnirelmann density $\alpha$
and every $N$ there exists $b \in B$ such that
$$
  \lvert (A \cup (A+b)) \cap \{1, \ldots, N\} \rvert \geq (\alpha + f(\alpha)) N
$$
where $f(\alpha) > 0$ for $0 < \alpha < 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #424
research_problems.statement:
Defines the set of new numbers generated from a set A by the operation
$x y - 1$ for $x \neq y$.

Let $a_1 = 2$ and $a_2 = 3$ and continue the sequence by appending to $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ all possible
values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.
Is it true that the set of integers which eventually appear has positive density?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1061
research_problems.statement:
How many (ordered) solutions are there to `σ(a) + σ(b) = σ(a + b)` with `a + b ≤ x`?
Is it true that this number is asymptotic to `c * x` for some constant `c > 0`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #821
research_problems.statement:
Let $g(n)$ count the number of $m$ such that $\phi(m)=n$.

Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ such that
$g(n) > n^{1-\epsilon}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #897
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

(b) Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n f(n+1)/ f(n) = ∞$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #420
research_problems.statement:
(a) If $\tau(n)$ counts the number of divisors of $n$ then let
$$F(f,n)=\frac{\tau((n+\lfloor f(n)\rfloor)!)}{\tau(n!)}.$$
Is it true that
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}F((\log n)^C,n)=\infty$$
for large $C$?

(b) Is it true that $F(\log n,n)$ is everywhere dense in $(1,\infty)$?

(c) More generally, if $f(n)\leq \log n$ is a monotonic function such that $f(n)\to \infty$ as
$n\to \infty$, then is $F(f,n)$ everywhere dense?

research_problems.statement: Let $h(k)$ be Jacobsthal's function, defined to as the minimal $m$ such that, if $n$ has at most $k$ prime factors, then in any set of $m$ consecutive integers there exists an integer coprime to $n$. Determine the order of magnitude of $h(k)$. In particular, is it true that $$h(k) \ll k^2?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #50
research_problems.statement:
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #952
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$
such that $\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1146
research_problems.statement:
We say that $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is an essential component if $d_s(A \oplus B)>d_s(B)$ for every
$B\subset \mathbb{N}$ with $0<d_s(B)<1$ where $d_s$ is the Schnirelmann density.
Here, the sumset is the appropriate one for Schnirelmann density, $A \oplus B = \{a+b \mid a \in A \cup \{0\}, b \in B \cup \{0\}\}$ (i.e. $(A \cup \{0\}) + (B \cup \{0\})$).
This avoids the trivial case where the sumset misses $1$ simply because neither $A$ nor $B$ contains $0$.

Is $B=\{2^m3^n : m,n\geq 0\}$ an essential component?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #472
research_problems.statement:
Given a finite sequence of primes $q_1<\cdots<q_m$, extend it by taking $q_{n+1}$ to be the
smallest prime of the form $q_n+q_i-1$ for $n\geq m$. Is there an initial sequence for which
this process continues forever?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #537
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $N$ be sufficiently large. If $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
$\lvert A\rvert \geq \epsilon N$ then must there exist $a_1,a_2,a_3\in A$ and distinct primes
$p_1,p_2,p_3$ such that
$$a_1p_1=a_2p_2=a_3p_3?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #126
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?

research_problems.statement:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #394
research_problems.statement:
Let $t_k(n)$ denote the least $m$ such that $n\mid m(m+1)(m+2)\cdots (m+k-1).$

(a) Is it true that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{x^2}{(\log x)^c}$ for some $c>0$?

(b) Is it true that, for $k\geq 2$, $\sum_{n\leq x}t_{k+1}(n) =o\left(\sum_{n\leq x}t_k(n)\right)?$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #535
research_problems.statement:
Let $r \geq 3$, and let $f_r(N)$ denote the size of the largest subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$
such that no subset of size $r$ has the same pairwise greatest common divisor between all
elements. Erdős [Er64] proved that $f_3(N) > N^{c/\log\log N}$ for some constant $c > 0$, and
conjectured this should also be an upper bound; here we state the conjectural upper bound
for all $r \geq 3$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #362
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a finite set of size $N$. Is it true that, for any fixed $t$,
there are
$$\ll \frac{2^N}{N^{3/2}}$$
many $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}n=t$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1122
research_problems.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}$ be an additive function (i.e. $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$ whenever
$(a,b)=1$). Let
$$A=\{ n \geq 1: f(n+1)< f(n)\}.$$
If $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert =o(X)$ then must $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in \mathbb{R}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #25
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #493
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist a $k$ such that every sufficiently large integer can be written in the form
$$\prod_{i=1}^k a_i - \sum_{i=1}^k a_i$$
for some integers $a_i\geq 2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1110
research_problems.statement:
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers, that is, an infinite
family of pairwise coprime non-representable integers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #363
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for each fixed $n$ and fixed sizes $k_1,\ldots,k_n \geq 4$, there are only finitely
many collections of disjoint intervals $I_1,\ldots,I_n$ of size $\lvert I_i\rvert = k_i$ for

(a) Let $f(m)$ be such that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has $\lvert A\rvert=m$ then every interval
in $[1,\infty)$ of length $2N$ contains $\geq f(m)$ many distinct integers $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ where

research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for every $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the largest prime
divisor of
$$
  \prod_{i = 0}^k (p ^ 2 + i)
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #418
research_problems.statement: Are there infinitely many integers not of the form $n - \phi(n)$?

Define a sequence by $a_1=1$ and $$a_{n+1}=\lfloor\sqrt{2}(a_n+1/2)\rfloor$$ for $n\geq 1$.

Define $\epsilon_n$ to be maximal such that there exists some choice of congruence class $a_p$

research_problems.statement:
Let $a$ be some sequence of natural numbers. We set $F(A,X,k)$ to be the count of
the number of $i$ such that $[a_i,a_{i+1}, \dots ,a_{i+k−1}] < X$,

Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and let $F(A,X,k)$ count the number of $i$

Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. Show that the set of $n$
with $P(n+1) > P(n)$ has density $\frac{1}{2}$.

research_problems.statement:
Let $p_n$ be the smallest prime $\equiv 1\pmod{n}$.

Let $m_n$ be the smallest integer such that $n\mid \phi(m_n)$.

(a) Is it true that $m_n<p_n$ for almost all $n$?

(b) Does $p_n/m_n \to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

Is there a permutation $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ of the positive integers such that $a_k + a_{k+1}$ is

research_problems.statement:

research_problems.statement:
Let $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \ldots$ be the Farey fractions of order $n \geq 4$. Let

research_problems.statement:
Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. There are infinitely many $n$ such that
$P(n)>P(n+1)>P(n+2)$.

research_problems.statement:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?

research_problems.statement:

least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier $a_j$s. Show that $a_k / k \to \infty$.

(b) Let $a_1< a_2 < ⋯ $ be an infinite sequence of integers such that $a_1=1$ and $a_{i+1}$ is the
least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier $a_j$s. Show that $a_k / k ^ {1 + c} \to 0$
for any $c > 0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #208
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
for any $\epsilon > 0$ and large $n$, $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll_\epsilon s_n^\epsilon$?

(b) Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
$s_{n + 1} - s_n \le (1 + o(1)) \cdot (\pi^2 / 6) \cdot \log (s_n) / \log (\log (s_n))$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #389
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for every $n \geq 1$ there is a $k$ such that
$$
  n(n + 1) \cdots (n + k - 1) \mid (n + k) \cdots (n + 2k - 1)?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #829
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the set of perfect cubes.  Is
it true that $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \ll (\log n)^{O(1)}$?  That is, does there exist a natural
number $C$ such that the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1062
research_problems.statement:
Erdős asked whether the limiting density `f n / n` exists and, if so, whether it is
irrational.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #457
research_problems.statement:
Is there some $\epsilon > 0$ such that there are infinitely
many $n$ where all primes $p \le (2 + \epsilon) \log n$ divide
$$
  \prod_{1 \le i \le \log n} (n + i)?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #686
research_problems.statement:
Can every integer $N≥2$ be written as
$$N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #453
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $i<n$ such that
$$
p_n^2 < p_{n+i}p_{n-i},
$$
where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #489
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set such that $\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert=o(x^{1/2})$. Let
$B=\{ n\geq 1 : a\nmid n\textrm{ for all }a\in A\}$.
If $B=\{b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ then is it true that
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{b_i < x}(b_{i+1}-b_i)^2$$
exists (and is finite)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #480
research_problems.statement:
Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots\in [0,1]$ be an infinite sequence.
Is it true that
$$\inf_n \liminf_{m\to \infty} n \lvert x_{m+n}-x_m\rvert\leq 5^{-1/2}\approx 0.447?$$
A conjecture of Newman.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #770
research_problems.statement:
Let $h n$ be the minimal number such that $2 ^ n - 1, \dots, h(n) ^ n - 1$
are collectively coprime.

(a) For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist?

(b) Does `liminf h n = ∞`?

(c) Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #839
research_problems.statement:
(a) Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?

(b) Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #416
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable. Does `V(2x)/V(x)→2` ?

(b) Let `V(x)` count the number of `n≤x` such that `ϕ(m)=n` is solvable.
Is there an asymptotic formula for `V(x)`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #536
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $N$ be sufficiently large. Is it true that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\epsilon N$ then there must be distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that
$$[a, b]=[b, c]=[a, c],$$
where $[\cdot, \cdot]$ denotes the least common multiple?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #369
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there is a
sequence of $k$ consecutive integers in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ all of which are $n^\epsilon$-smooth?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1057
research_problems.statement:
Let $C(x)$ count the number of Carmichael numbers in the interval $[1,x]$.

Is it true that $C(x)=x^{1-o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #978
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2`, is not equal to a power of `2`, and `f n` has no fixed
`(k - 1)`-th power divisors other than `1`. Then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th
power free has positive density, and this is proved in [Ho67].

(b) If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?

(c) Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #540
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ has size $\gg N^{1/2}$ then there exists
some non-empty $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}n\equiv 0\pmod{N}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #487
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such
that $[a,b]=c$ (where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #479
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every integer $k\neq 1$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$2^n\equiv k\pmod{n}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #976
research_problems.statement:
Let $f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$. Let $F_f(n)$ be maximal
such that there exists $1\leq m\leq n$ with $f(m)$ is divisible by a prime $\geq F_f(n)$.
Equivalently, $F_f(n)$ is the greatest prime divisor of
$$\prod_{1\leq m\leq n}f(m).$$
Estimate $F_f(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #981
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and $f_\epsilon(p)$ be the smallest integer $m$
such that $\sum_{n\leq N} \left(\frac{n}{p}\right)<\epsilon N$ for all $N\geq m$. Prove that
$$\sum_{p<x}f_\epsilon(p)\sim c_\epsilon \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some $c_\epsilon > 0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #774
research_problems.statement:
We call $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ dissociated if $\sum_{n\in X}n\neq \sum_{m\in Y}m$
for all finite $X,Y\subset A$ with $X\neq Y$.

We call $A$ proportionately dissociated if every finite $B\subset A$
contains a dissociated set of size $\gg \lvert B\rvert$.

In other words, there is a (global) $c > 0$ such that every finite $B \subset A$
contains a dissociated set of size $\geq c|B|$.

Is every proportionately dissociated (infinite) set the union of a finite
number of dissociated sets?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #538
research_problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$ and suppose that $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is such that, for any
$m$, there are at most $r$ solutions to $m=pa$ where $p$ is prime and $a\in A$.
Give the best possible upper bound for $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #649
research_problems.statement:
Let $P(m)$ denote the greatest prime factor of $m$. Is it true that, for any two primes $p,q$,
there exists some integer $n$ such that $P(n)=p$ and $P(n+1)=q$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #711
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n,m)$ be minimal such that $(m,m+f(n,m))$ contains distinct integers
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with $k \mid a_k$ for $1 \leq k \leq n$. Prove that
$\max_m f(n,m) \leq n^{1+o(1)}$.

(b) Prove that $\max_m (f(n,m)-f(n,n)) \to \infty$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #691
research_problems.statement:
Given $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, let
$M_A = \{n \geq 1 : a \mid n \text{ for some } a \in A\}$. Find a necessary and sufficient
condition on $A$ for $M_A$ to have density $1$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1058
research_problems.statement:
Let $2=p_1<p_2<\cdots$ be the sequence of prime numbers. Are there only finitely many $n$ such
that $n\in [p_{k-1},p_k)$ and the only primes dividing $n!+1$ are $p_{k}$ and $p_{k+1}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #481
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{i}\frac{1}{a_i}>1$. For any
finite sequence of $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integers $A=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ let $T(A)$ denote
the sequence of length $rn$ given by
$$(a_ix_j+b_i)_{1\leq j\leq n, 1\leq i\leq r}.$$
Prove that, if $A_1=(1)$ and $A_{i+1}=T(A_i)$, then there must be some $A_k$ with repeated
elements.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #824
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(x)$ count the number of integers $1\leq a<b<x$ such that $(a,b)=1$ and
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma$ is the sum of divisors function. Is it true that
$h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #972
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #676
research_problems.statement:
Is every sufficiently large integer of the form $ap^2+b$ for some prime $p$ and integers
$a \geq 1$ and $0 \leq b < p$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1052
research_problems.statement: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #689
research_problems.statement:
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?

Let $n \geq 1$ and
$$A = \{a_1 < \cdots < a_{\phi(n)}\} = \{1 \leq m < n : (m, n) = 1\}.$$
Is it true that
$$\sum_{1 \leq k < \phi(n)} (a_{k+1} - a_k)^2 \ll \frac{n^2}{\phi(n)}?$$

all primes $p\leq x$ such that every integer in $[1,y]$ is congruent to at least one of the
$a_p\pmod{p}$. Give good estimates for $Y(x)$.

(c) Or, even stronger, can one prove that $Y(x)\ll x^{1+o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1073
research_problems.statement:
Let $A(x)$ count the number of composite $u < x$ such that $n!+1 \equiv 0 (\mod u)$ for some $n$.

Is it true that $A(x) \le x^{o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #828
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #490
research_problems.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that all the products $ab$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$
are distinct. Is it true that
$$\lvert A\rvert \lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{N^2}{\log N}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #985
research_problems.statement: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #253
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dotsc$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that
$\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i} \to 1$. If every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many
integers which are the sum of distinct $a_i$ then every sufficiently large integer is
the sum of distinct $a_i$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #361
research_problems.statement:
For fixed $c$ and $n$, this is the size of the largest set
$A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, \lfloor cn \rfloor\}$ such that no subset of $A$ sums to $n$.

Let $c > 0$ and $n$ be some large integer. What is the size of the largest set
$A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, \lfloor c n \rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of a subset of $A$?
Does this depend on $n$ in an irregular way?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #830
research_problems.statement:
Let $A(x)$ count the number of amicable pairs $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$.

(a) **Erdos Problem 830, Part 1**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?

(b) **Erdos Problem 830, Part 2**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #239
research_problems.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \{-1,1\}$ be a multiplicative function. Is it true that
$$ \lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N}f(n)$$ always exists?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #889
research_problems.statement:
Let $v(n,k)$ count the prime factors of $n+k$ which
do not divide $n+i$ for $0\leq i < k$. Is it true that
$v_0(n)=\max_{k\geq 0}v(n,k)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #429
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, if $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is sparse enough and does not cover all residue
classes modulo $p$ for any prime $p$, then there exists some $n\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $n+a$ is
prime for all $a\in A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #422
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(1) = f(2) = 1$ and for $n > 2$
$$
f(n) = f(n - f(n - 1)) + f(n - f(n - 2)).
$$
Does $f(n)$ miss infinitely many integers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #382
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $u \leq v$ be such that the largest prime dividing $\prod_{u \leq m \leq v} m$ appears with
exponent at least $2$. Is it true that $v - u = v^{o(1)}$?

(b) Let $u \leq v$ be such that the largest prime dividing $\prod_{u \leq m \leq v} m$ appears with
exponent at least $2$. Can $v - u$ be arbitrarily large?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #51
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $a \in A$,
there is an integer n such that $\phi(n)=a$, and
yet if $n_a$ is the smallest such integer, then $\frac{n_a}{a} → \infty$ as $a → ∞$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1004
research_problems.statement:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1136
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ with lower density $>1/3$ such that $a+b\neq 2^k$ for
any $a,b\in A$ and $k\geq 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1056
research_problems.statement:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1072
research_problems.statement:
For any prime $p$, let $f(p)$ be the least integer such that $f(p)! + 1 \equiv 0 \mod p$.

(a) Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$?

(b) Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #421
research_problems.statement:
There exists a sequence $1 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots$ with density 1 such that all products
$\prod_{u \le i \le v} d_i$ are distinct. This was solved affirmatively; see [Pratt26].

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #694
research_problems.statement:
Let $f_\max(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that $\phi(m) = n$, and
$f_\min(n)$ be the smallest such $m$, where $\phi$ is Euler's
totient function. Investigate
$$
  \max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)}.
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1209
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a sequence of integers which tends to infinity sufficiently fast.
If there is an $n$ such that all $n+a_k$ are primes then must there exist infinitely many such $n$?

(b) What if we ask for $n+a_k$ to be squarefree instead of prime?

(c) Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always a prime?

(d) Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always squarefree?

(e) Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often a prime?

(f) Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is infinitely often squarefree?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #13
research_problems.statement:
If $A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ is a set with no $a, b, c \in A$ such that $a | (b+c)$ and
$a < \min(b,c)$, then $|A| \le N/3 + O(1)$. This has been solved by Bedert [Be23].

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1214
research_problems.statement:
Let $x,y\geq 1$ be integers such that, for all $n\geq 1$, the set of primes dividing $x^{n}-1$ is
equal to the set of primes dividing $y^n-1$. Must $x=y$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1149
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha>0$ be a real number, not an integer. The density of integers $n\geq 1$ for which
$(n,\lfloor n^\alpha\rfloor)=1$ is $6/\pi^2$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #826
research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #822
research_problems.statement: Does the set of integers of the form $n + \varphi(n)$ have positive (lower) density?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #435
research_problems.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\neq p^k$ for any prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. What is the largest
integer not of the form
$$\sum_{1\leq i<n}c_i\binom{n}{i}$$
where the $c_i\geq 0$ are integers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1065
research_problems.statement:
(a) Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k * q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$?

(b) Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k 3^l q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$, $l ≥ 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #437
research_problems.statement:
Let $1\leq a_1<\cdots<a_k\leq x$. How many of the partial products
$a_1,a_1a_2,\ldots,a_1\cdots a_k$ can be squares? Is it true that, for any $\epsilon>0$, there can
be more than $x^{1-\epsilon}$ squares?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #445
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for any $c>1/2$, if $p$ is a sufficiently large prime then, for any
$n\geq 0$, there exist $a,b\in(n,n+p^c)$ such that $ab\equiv 1\pmod{p}$?

research_problems.statement:

$F(n)\gg n\log\log n$?

(d) Is it true that, for all large $x$, $\max_{n\le x}f(n)=\max_{n\le x}F(n)$?

(e) Find an asymptotic formula for the number of $n<x$ such that $f(n)=F(n)$.

(f) Find an asymptotic formula for $H(x)=\sum_{n<x}f(n)/n$.

(g) Is it true that $H(x)\ll x\log\log\log\log x$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #955
research_problems.statement:

If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has density $0$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ must also have density $0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #845
research_problems.statement:
Let $C > 0$. Is it true that the set of integers of the form $n = b_1 + \cdots + b_t$,
with $b_1 < \cdots < b_t$, where $b_i = 2^{k_i}3^{l_i}$ for $1 \leq i\leq t$ and

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #710
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that in $(n,n+f(n))$ there exist distinct integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$
such that $k\mid a_k$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$. Obtain an asymptotic formula for $f(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1210
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq [1,n)$ be a set of integers such that $(a,b)=1$ for all distinct $a,b\in A$.
Is it true that $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{n-a}\leq \sum_{p < n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)$?

research_problems.statement:
Let $N(X,\delta)$ denote the maximum number of points $P_1,\ldots,P_n$ which can be chosen in a
circle of radius $X$ such that
$$\| \lvert P_i-P_j\rvert \| \geq \delta$$
for all $1\leq i<j\leq n$. (Here $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer.)

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #436
research_problems.statement:
(a) If $p$ is a prime and $k, m \geq 2$, let $r(k, m, p)$ be the minimal $r$ such that
$r, r + 1, \ldots, r + m - 1$ are all $k$th power residues modulo $p$, and let

research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n + k) \ll k$ for all $k \geq 1$?
Here $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #771
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, for every $m\geq 1$, there exists some
$S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert S\rvert=f(n)$ such that $m\neq \sum_{a\in A}a$ for all
$A\subseteq S$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) = \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)\frac{n}{\log n}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #709
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that, for any $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\subseteq [2,\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$
of size $n$, in any interval $I$ of $f(n)\max(A)$ consecutive integers there exist distinct
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$ such that $a_i\mid x_i$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1053
research_problems.statement:
Call a number $k$-perfect if $\sigma(n)=kn$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the divisors
of $n$. Must $k=o(\log\log n)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #388
research_problems.statement:
Are there only finitely many solutions of
$$\prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(m_1+i)=\prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2}(m_2+j)$$
with $k_1,k_2>3$ and $m_1+k_1\leq m_2$?
